evidence.text: The entry analyzes 爺 as 从父、耶聲, with original sense “father.” It cites Mulan Poetry for the father sense, Old Book of Tang for an honorific use, a Taiping Heavenly Kingdom proclamation for a divine honorific, and a Ming Wan-shu za-ji quotation “祖曰爺” for grandfather. These are dictionary-reported citations; they do not establish the dates of the earliest surviving witnesses or the sequence of semantic change.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the CUHK character entry and Wiktionary’s Zhengzhang summary. All four direct Unihan lookups returned internal errors. The MOE page and CNS11643 page were returned in search results, but opening them failed; their snippets were not treated as inspected-page evidence.

gaps: No verified dated inscription, manuscript image, or palaeographic sequence for 爺 was obtained. First formation date and any specific seal-to-clerical path remain unresolved.

The CUHK entry’s dated literary citations were not checked against primary editions or manuscript witnesses. Earliest attested forms and exact chronology of father, honorific, divine-honorific, and grandfather senses remain uncertain; semantic transitions are not established.

The modern Mandarin readings in supplied local rows (耶 yé and 爺 yé) are metadata only. The official per-character Unihan pages could not be inspected in this turn. Zhengzhang /*laː/ is available here only through a secondary summary; no primary reconstruction volume was inspected. The local Baxter–Sagart rows provided cover 父 only, not 耶 or 爺, so no Baxter–Sagart comparison can be supplied.
No evidence found that 爺 itself is a corrupted graph or a whole-graph phonetic loan. A separate claim about 耶’s graphic history would not establish corruption of 爺.

The exact entry 爺→爷 in a primary simplified-character standard was not verified. The inspected CUHK record identifies their traditional/simplified correspondence, but its entry does not supply the primary standardization table row.

The dossier’s Old Turkic comparison and the original word/object behind any proposed borrowing were not independently verified; do not treat the phonetic-component analysis as a whole-graph loan claim.
